content.summary: Read about fast fashion, impulse buying and ways to shop more thoughtfully. You will find the main ideas and details, then use must be and can't be to make strong guesses from evidence.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Use must be to say something is almost certainly true, and can't be to say something is almost certainly not true. Use must be + -ing to make a deduction about an activity happening now.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words about shopping choices, clothing production, working conditions and the environment.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim each paragraph to understand its main idea. Then scan for names, numbers and reasons that answer specific questions. Use details in the text as evidence for a deduction.

learningObjectives: Understand the main ideas in a B1 text about fast fashion and conscious shopping.
Find details about shopping habits, clothing production and environmental effects.
Use must be and can't be to make deductions from information in a text.

contextWarmup.prompt: You see a T-shirt advertised at a very low price. What is a reasonable first thought?
options: The production costs must be low.
The T-shirt can't be made from any material.
The shop must be closed.
contextWarmup.explanation: A very low price can suggest low production costs, although you would need more information to know how the shirt was made.

rules: Use must be + a noun or adjective when evidence makes you almost certain about something now: The price must be very low because the fabric is thin.
Use can't be + a noun or adjective when you are almost certain something is not true: This can't be a fair price for the workers.
Use must be + verb-ing to make a strong guess about an activity happening now: They must be buying clothes because the sale signs are everywhere.

commonTrap.explanation: Must be and can't be express a strong deduction. They are not the same as talking about an obligation. After must be, use a noun or adjective, or use a verb ending in -ing.
commonTrap.wrong: The workers must are earning very little.
commonTrap.correct: The workers must be earning very little.

content.passageTitle: A Better Way to Fill Your Wardrobe
paragraphs: On Saturday, Mia went shopping with her friend Leo. A shop window showed a T-shirt for two dollars, and Mia wanted to buy three. Leo asked if she really needed them. Mia looked at the thin fabric and the low price. The T-shirts must be made very cheaply, she thought, but she did not know who had made them.

Later, they read about fast fashion. Some brands make new collections every few weeks, so shoppers feel pressure to follow new trends. Clothes may be cheap, but making and moving them can add to the industry's carbon footprint. In some factories, workers face long hours and low pay. A low price alone cannot tell Mia exactly where a garment came from.

Mia decided to pause before buying anything. She checked the labels and found no clear information about the factory. The shop could not answer her questions about the workers, either. The T-shirts can't be a fully responsible choice if the shop cannot explain how they were made, she decided. That did not prove that the factory was unfair, but it gave her a reason to be careful.

Instead, Mia and Leo visited a second-hand shop. Mia found a strong jacket that fitted well, and Leo bought a shirt he had been looking for. At home, Mia repaired a loose button on one of her old tops. She realised that conscious shopping does not mean never buying anything. It means thinking about what you need, how long an item will last, and what you can learn about its production.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Shop with Your Eyes Open

content.summary: Use must be and can't be to make strong guesses from evidence about shopping and fashion. Use must be + -ing to guess what someone is doing now. Build a clear paragraph by stating your point, adding evidence, and explaining your conclusion.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Make a Positive Deduction
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + must be + noun or adjective
blueprintItems.example: The jacket costs only five dollars, so the fabric must be very cheap.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Make a Negative Deduction
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + can't be + noun or adjective
blueprintItems.example: This coat falls apart after one wash, so it can't be good quality.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Guess What Is Happening Now
blueprintItems.example: The store is full of people, so it must be having a big sale.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use must be or can't be before a noun or an adjective when you make a strong guess.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: These shoes must be good quality.
mechanicsRules.why: The verb be is needed after must before a noun or adjective.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a verb ending in -ing after must be when you guess that an action is happening now.
mechanicsRules.badExample: She must be buy more clothes.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: She must be buying more clothes.
mechanicsRules.why: Must be + verb-ing describes a likely action happening now.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use can't be for a strong negative deduction, and do not add not after can't.
mechanicsRules.badExample: This bag can't not be made well.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: This bag can't be made well.
mechanicsRules.why: Can't already makes the deduction negative.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Smart Spending and Conscious Fashion

content.summary: Learn how to express strong logical deductions about shopping habits and fast fashion using modal verbs like 'must be' and 'can't be'. Practice placing stress on key information and maintaining smooth linking across compound nouns.
content.audioGuidance: When making deductions, put vocal weight on the modal verb or the following adjective to signal certainty. Keep function words unstressed and connect ending consonants to beginning vowels naturally.

pillars.name: Modal Deduction Stress
pillars.explanation: In sentences like 'That price can't be right' or 'She must be an impulse buyer', emphasize 'can't' or 'must' to show how certain you feel about the situation.

pillars.name: Compound Noun Rhythm
pillars.target: Front-stress on shopping and environmental terms
pillars.explanation: Compound nouns like 'sweatshop', 'fast fashion', and 'carbon footprint' usually carry the primary stress on the first element.

pillars.name: Vowel Contrast in Modals
pillars.explanation: Use a clear long vowel for 'can't' with a crisp final /t/ to avoid confusing it with the weak form of 'can'.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that 'conscious' stresses the first syllable, whereas 'consumption' shifts stress to the second syllable.
The root stress stays on 'TAIN' even when the suffix '-able' is added.
As a noun, the stress is on the first syllable, but as an action verb, it moves to the second syllable.
The stress jumps to the third syllable 'NO' before the suffix '-ic'.

reading.question: Why did Mia first want to buy three T-shirts?
options: They were being sold for a very low price.
Leo asked her to buy them.
She needed them for work.
reading.answer: They were being sold for a very low price.
reading.explanation: The passage says Mia saw a T-shirt for two dollars and wanted to buy three.

reading.question: What did Leo ask Mia?
options: Whether she really needed the T-shirts.
Whether she had visited the shop before.
Whether she wanted to work in a factory.
reading.answer: Whether she really needed the T-shirts.
reading.explanation: Leo asked if Mia really needed the three T-shirts.

reading.question: What does the passage say fast-fashion brands may do?
options: Make new collections every few weeks.
Sell only second-hand clothes.
Stop making clothes during new trends.
reading.answer: Make new collections every few weeks.
reading.explanation: The second paragraph says some brands make new collections every few weeks.

reading.question: What can making and moving clothes add to?
options: The industry's carbon footprint.
The number of factory workers.
The age of a garment.
reading.explanation: The passage connects making and moving clothes with the industry's carbon footprint.

reading.question: What does the passage say about workers in some factories?
options: They may face long hours and low pay.
They always choose their own working hours.
They only make second-hand clothes.
reading.answer: They may face long hours and low pay.
reading.explanation: The passage states that workers in some factories face long hours and low pay.

reading.question: Why did Mia become careful about buying the T-shirts?
options: The label gave no clear factory information, and the shop could not answer her questions.
The T-shirts did not have a price.
Leo said that all cheap clothes are badly made.
reading.answer: The label gave no clear factory information, and the shop could not answer her questions.
reading.explanation: Mia found no clear information on the label, and the shop could not answer questions about the workers.

reading.question: What did Mia's deduction that the T-shirts must be made very cheaply mean?
options: She thought the low price was evidence of very low production costs.
She knew exactly who had made the T-shirts.
She thought the T-shirts were second-hand.
reading.answer: She thought the low price was evidence of very low production costs.
reading.explanation: Mia made a strong guess from the thin fabric and low price, but she did not know who had made the shirts.

reading.question: What did Mia buy at the second-hand shop?
options: A strong jacket that fitted well.
Three new T-shirts.
A pair of factory shoes.
reading.answer: A strong jacket that fitted well.
reading.explanation: The final paragraph says Mia found a strong jacket that fitted well.

reading.question: What did Mia repair at home?
options: A loose button on an old top.
A tear in her new jacket.
A broken shop window.
reading.answer: A loose button on an old top.
reading.explanation: Mia repaired a loose button on one of her old tops.

reading.question: According to the passage, what does conscious shopping involve?
options: Thinking about what you need, how long an item will last and how it was made.
Never buying clothes again.
Buying the newest trend as soon as it appears.
reading.answer: Thinking about what you need, how long an item will last and how it was made.
reading.explanation: The final sentence describes considering need, how long an item will last and what you can learn about its production.

reading.question: According to the workplace policy, what is the primary consequence of missing a project milestone?
options: The project lead must submit a revised timeline and conduct a risk assessment.
The entire development team is immediately replaced by external contractors.
All project funding is automatically cancelled without further review.
Clients are notified only after the product is officially deployed.
reading.answer: The project lead must submit a revised timeline and conduct a risk assessment.
reading.explanation: Standard corporate policy dictates remediation through timeline review and risk mitigation.

reading.question: Which connector indicates a contrast between two independent clauses?
options: Nevertheless
Furthermore
Consequently
Similarly
reading.explanation: 'Nevertheless' signals contrast or concession, equivalent to 'however'.

reading.question: What does the author imply by stating 'the transition required considerable organizational agility'?
options: The company had to adapt rapidly to unexpected structural changes.
Employees refused to learn modern technological software.
The executive leadership considered the project an outright failure.
No further organizational adjustments would be necessary in the future.
reading.answer: The company had to adapt rapidly to unexpected structural changes.
reading.explanation: 'Agility' signifies the capacity to pivot and respond flexibly to change.

reading.question: Identify the sentence that correctly utilizes the Third Conditional:
options: If we had anticipated the market demand, we would have expanded production sooner.
If we anticipate the market demand, we will expand production.
If we had anticipated the market demand, we will have expanded production.
If we anticipated the market demand, we would expand production sooner.
reading.answer: If we had anticipated the market demand, we would have expanded production sooner.
reading.explanation: Third conditional formula: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

reading.question: Why did the client request an amendment to the contractual agreement?
options: To ensure delivery milestones aligned with their internal quarterly budget cycles.
Because they intended to terminate all business relations immediately.
To eliminate all warranty protections and technical support clauses.
Because the initial contract was drafted without legal counsel.
reading.answer: To ensure delivery milestones aligned with their internal quarterly budget cycles.
reading.explanation: Contract amendments in B2 business scenarios typically align scope with financial planning.

writing.instruction: Rewrite the sentence as a strong positive deduction using must be.
writing.promptText: The low price suggests that the fabric is cheap.
targetAnswers: The fabric must be cheap.
writing.explanation: Use must be to show a strong conclusion based on the low price.

writing.instruction: Rewrite the sentence as a strong negative deduction using can't be.
writing.promptText: These shoes are not good quality. They fall apart after one day.
writing.hint: Begin with: These shoes can't be...
targetAnswers: These shoes can't be good quality.
writing.explanation: The shoes falling apart is evidence for the strong negative deduction.

writing.instruction: Join the ideas using must be + verb-ing.
writing.promptText: The shop is full of customers. It is having a sale.
targetAnswers: The shop must be having a sale.
writing.explanation: Use must be + verb-ing to guess what is happening now.

writing.instruction: Complete the sentence with a conjunction that shows a result.
writing.promptText: The jacket is very cheap, ___ it must be made from low-cost materials.
targetAnswers: so
writing.explanation: So introduces a result that follows from the low price.

writing.instruction: Complete the sentence with a conjunction that shows contrast.
writing.promptText: The shirt is expensive, ___ its label says it is made from poor materials.
targetAnswers: but
writing.explanation: But joins two ideas that contrast with each other.

writing.instruction: Complete the sentence with a conjunction that gives a reason.
writing.promptText: I will not buy the coat ___ its seams are already coming apart.
targetAnswers: because
writing.explanation: Because introduces the reason for not buying the coat.

writing.promptText: this brand must be popular it has a long queue
writing.hint: Use capital letters and make two complete sentences or join the ideas with a conjunction.
targetAnswers: This brand must be popular. It has a long queue.
This brand must be popular because it has a long queue.
This brand must be popular, as it has a long queue.
writing.explanation: Begin with a capital letter and use punctuation to separate complete ideas.

writing.instruction: Correct the grammar, capitalization, and punctuation.
writing.promptText: those bags cant be made from real leather
writing.hint: Capitalize the first word and add the apostrophe in can't.
targetAnswers: Those bags can't be made from real leather.
writing.explanation: Start the sentence with a capital letter, spell can't with an apostrophe, and end with a full stop.

writing.instruction: Write two sentences about the evidence and your deduction.
writing.promptText: A shopper has four new coats and is still looking at more clothes. What must she be doing?
writing.hint: Use must be + verb-ing and give a reason.
targetAnswers: She must be shopping for clothes. She has several new coats and is looking for more.
She must be buying more clothes because she already has four new coats.
writing.explanation: A clear response makes a deduction with must be + verb-ing and supports it with evidence from the prompt.

writing.instruction: Write two or three sentences giving your opinion and a deduction.

writing.explanation: Give a reasonable deduction from the evidence and add a relevant action before making a purchase.
